summary: The 200K cameraman clip at 6,809 views is still the dominant benchmark and its formula is clear: a specific surprising number named in the hook banner at the top of the frame, the spoken punchline echoed as large 2-3 word upper-case subtitles, a clean two-person reaction shot in blur-fill, and a hard cut to the moment on frame one — all resolved in 20 seconds or less. The 1,152–1,295 view cluster shares a universal awkwardness or physical comedy angle (stranger challenge, embarrassing hot take, cops catching you repeatedly) that lands with zero prior context. Titles that open with a concrete detail — a number, a named situation, a quoted line — consistently outperform vague titles. moments_to_pick: Cartier says a specific number out loud — a salary, a price, a count, a year — that will surprise a first-time viewer with zero context
A stranger physically does something unexpected with Cartier or crew: a skill demo, a challenge accepted, a confrontation that resolves on camera
An unscripted social exchange turns awkward — someone gets clowned, a compliment lands wrong, an unexpected reveal mid-conversation
Cartier delivers a confident hot take about a celebrity, a game, a food, or a job that sounds absurd but he defends it with a straight face
Chat reaction triggers visible Cartier silence then laughter — the reaction IS the clip, nothing else needed
A gross or embarrassing physical moment followed immediately by a wild excuse or justification from Cartier

title_formula: Open with the specific surprising detail — a number, a quoted phrase, a named situation — in plain English, then add the reaction or consequence in 3-6 words, close with one emoji. Never start with 'Cartier2Real' as the first word; lead with the detail. Keep under 70 characters. Example: '200K a yea
caption_formula: Line 1: One punchy sentence that rewords the hook as a reaction or commentary — do not copy the title. Line 2: One sentence teasing the payoff from Cartier's angle without fully spoiling it. Line 3: 'Catch Cartier live on Kick: kick.com/cartier2real' with @cartier2real tag. Example — Line 1: 'Nobody
avoid: Any establishing shot, slow pan or silent intro before the punchline — cut directly to the moment on frame one
Clips over 25 seconds unless a physical or social arc is impossible to understand without the full build — absolute hard cap at 35s
Vague titles with no concrete detail: 'Cartier reacts to something crazy' names nothing — always lead with the specific thing that happened
Currency symbols anywhere in titles, captions or on-screen text (campaign rule)
Full ALL-CAPS hook text banners — sentence case on the top bar matches the best-performing clip and reads better on mobile
Repeating the same emoji in both the title and the hook banner — vary them
